hook.say: The ten tallest mountains in the lower forty-eight, ranked. Seven are in Colorado!

items.name: Crestone Peak
items.say: Number ten: Crestone Peak, one of Colorado's hardest. 14300 feet.
items.cap: Number ten: Crestone Peak, one of Colorado's hardest. 14,300 feet.

items.name: Uncompahgre Peak
items.say: Nine: Un-cum-pah-gray Peak, roof of the San Juans. 14321 feet.
items.cap: Nine: Uncompahgre Peak, roof of the San Juans. 14,321 feet.

items.name: La Plata Peak
items.say: Eight: La Plata Peak, its name means silver. 14343 feet.
items.cap: Eight: La Plata Peak, its name means silver. 14,343 feet.

items.name: Blanca Peak
items.say: Seven: Blanca Peak, sacred to the Navajo. 14351 feet.
items.cap: Seven: Blanca Peak, sacred to the Navajo. 14,351 feet.

items.name: Mt. Williamson
items.say: Six: Mount Williamson, California's second highest. 14379 feet.
items.cap: Six: Mt. Williamson, California's second highest. 14,379 feet.

items.name: Mount Rainier
items.say: Five: Mount Ruh-neer, a glacier-covered volcano. 14417 feet.
items.cap: Five: Mount Rainier, a glacier-covered volcano. 14,417 feet.

items.name: Mount Harvard
items.say: Four: Mount Harvard, named after the university. 14421 feet.
items.cap: Four: Mount Harvard, named after the university. 14,421 feet.

items.name: Mount Massive
items.say: Three: Mount Massive, with five separate summits. 14428 feet.
items.cap: Three: Mount Massive, with five separate summits. 14,428 feet.

items.name: Mount Elbert
items.say: Two: Mount Elbert, top of the Rockies. 14440 feet.
items.cap: Two: Mount Elbert, top of the Rockies. 14,440 feet.

items.name: Mount Whitney
items.say: And number one: Mount Whitney! 14505 feet, eighty-five miles from Death Valley.
items.cap: And number one: Mount Whitney! 14,505 feet, eighty-five miles from Death Valley.
